title: Isolation + SLA Decision Aid for Ops & Procurement Leads
content:
Purpose
This note is a compact decision aid and procurement-ready messaging kit for conversations with platform, security and procurement stakeholders evaluating dedicated inference capacity. It’s meant to be used by AE/SE/solutions during mid-cycle evaluation calls and by GtM leaders crafting RFP responses.

Audience
- Platform and infra architects evaluating capacity isolation and predictability
- InfoSec / Security teams assessing data residency and auditability
- Procurement teams negotiating SLA, credits, and termination clauses
- Product/ML teams validating latency and throughput guarantees for production features

High-level position / single-line pitch
"Dedicated capacity gives you predictable throughput and tail-latency SLOs with contractual isolation and operational arms for enterprise procurement — so product teams can ship LLM features to users without surprise throttles or noisy-neighbor disruptions."

Core pillars to emphasize (short bullets for customer meetings)
- Predictable throughput: guaranteed slots and capacity pools sized for your P50/P95 workload with clear burst policies.
- Tail-latency SLAs: P95/P99 latency targets by model class and sequence-length band, backed by service credits.
- Logical and physical isolation: tenant-level GPU pools, network segmentation (VPC peering / private link), private control plane, and optional on-prem packaging.
- Procurement-ready remediation: acceptance tests, defined service credits, migration assistance, and escalation paths.

Why this matters to ops/procurement
- Noisy neighbors blow up latency-sensitive features (autocomplete, real-time assistants). Predictable capacity = predictable UX and revenue.
- Security/compliance teams require both technical isolation (VPC, KMS) and contractual assurances (audit windows, retention policies).
- Procurement needs simple, testable acceptance criteria and remedies — not vague promises.

Suggested opening script for sales/SEs (30–60s)
"We provide a dedicated inference pool that’s isolated from other tenants and covered by explicit SLAs for both availability and tail latency. That means your product team gets stable per-token latency and throughput, and your security team gets network-level isolation and key control. For procurement, we publish acceptance test cases and a service-credit schedule so outages are measurable and contractable."

Differentiators vs. typical public-hosted endpoints
- Deterministic performance vs. opportunistic bursting: dedicated pools avoid queuing effects at tail latencies.
- End-to-end isolation: control plane separation, optional single-tenant runtime, and dedicated logging/audit exports.
- Enterprise-grade procurement: explicit performance SLAs tied to token latency/throughput bands and signed migration SLAs.

Competitive notes / rebuttals (short win-phrases)
- Competitor: "Our cheaper shared endpoint handles your traffic." Rebuttal: "Lower list price can hide variability; a single P99 spike can cost weeks of engineering time and user churn for real-time features."
- Competitor: "We offer private networking but no dedicated GPUs." Rebuttal: "Network isolation without compute isolation still leaves you vulnerable to noisy-neighbor tail latency."
- Competitor: "We provide indefinite best-effort support." Rebuttal: "We provide measurable, contractual remedies plus runbooks and a playbook for migration and incident resolution."

Procurement-ready clauses / sample language (cut-and-paste friendly)
- "Service Levels: Provider will maintain a P95 inference latency of <= X ms and P99 inference latency of <= Y ms for the agreed model/configuration over any calendar month, measured at the customer API ingress. If Provider fails to meet an SLA, Customer is eligible for service credits as defined below."
- "Throughput Guarantee: Provider will reserve N concurrent 'request slots' with sustained throughput of M tokens/second per slot. Bursting behavior is defined as an additional B slots with <Z% guaranteed availability per month."
- "Isolation & Data Controls: Dedicated instances will run on tenant-dedicated GPU pools with network segmentation (VPC peering or PrivateLink). Customer data at-rest will be encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS) upon request. Audit logs are exported to the customer’s logging endpoint with retention of T days."
- "Acceptance Test: During onboarding, Provider will run an acceptance test defined in Appendix A (20k sample requests across realistic sequence lengths). Failure to meet acceptance criteria allows Customer to withhold final payment and receive remediation within 14 days or opt for termination with migration assistance."
- "Remedies & Credits: Service credits scale with SLA shortfall tiers (e.g., 0.5% credit for single missed P95 objective, 5% credit for repeated or prolonged degradation)."

Operational evidence to include in RFPs and briefings
- SLO history: 12-month SLO attainment tables (availability and P95/P99 latency for model classes).
- Load-tested throughput matrix: tokens/sec per GPU profile (FP16 vs quantized) across sequence lengths.
- Incident playbook excerpt: communication cadence, runbook owner, and escalation matrix.
- Security artifacts: SOC2/ISO certs, KMS integration notes, private control plane architecture diagram.

Risk surface and mitigations to proactively address
- Risk: Model changes increase latency. Mitigation: pinned model versions for production routes and automatic fallback to a compatible, lower-latency variant with no config changes required.
- Risk: Burst traffic exceeds reserved capacity. Mitigation: configurable burst pools and auto-burst rate limits with pre-wired approval flows.
- Risk: Procurement wants unlimited credits or heavy termination levers. Mitigation: balance with reasonable remediation caps and a graduated remediation schedule; offer migration assistance and data export guarantees instead of unlimited penalties.

Price framing / negotiation anchors
- Anchor on unit economics: price per reserved slot per region + per-token delta. Show a worked example vs. best-effort public tier for 100M tokens/mo with 95% of requests under 1s P95.
- Offer a 3-month ramp credit: first 3 months at 10–20% discount while acceptance tests run and traffic ramps.

One-pager snippets for execs (short bullets)
- "Business impact: reduce user-facing latency variability by >90% for real-time LLM features; lowers production incidents caused by contention."
- "Procurement-ready: explicit acceptance tests, service credits, and migration assistance included in enterprise agreements."

Suggested next steps for field teams
1) Attach benchmark artifact for the specific model + expected sequence length.
2) Send the sample SLA language to procurement as a starting point.
3) Schedule a 30-min architecture call with SRE and security to validate isolation controls.
4) Offer a 30-day proof-of-concept with defined acceptance criteria.

Open questions to resolve (internal)
- Who authorizes the first-line acceptance test once onboarding completes? (SRE or Solutions?)
- Standard credit schedule thresholds and maximum liability cap for enterprise deals.
- Template for on-prem / air-gapped packaging exclusions and extra-cost items.

Appendix: quick checklist for deal desk and legal
- Confirm model version pinning and rollout policy clauses.
- Confirm KMS/customer key support and exportable logs.
- Ensure acceptance test metrics and tooling are attached as annex.
- Confirm incident escalation SLA and named contacts.

Notes / internal links
- See INF-DEDICATED-SLA-PLAYBOOK (Confluence) for detailed thresholds and historical SLO attainment.
- GTMP-4123: sales play for dedicated capacity (Jira) - includes POC checklist and template proposal text.

(Working draft — use snippets freely in RFP responses. Feedback from legal and SRE required before finalizing contract language.)
